answer: Each identity runs one reef buoy and locks a 75-credit bond. Its beacon posts positions, and a marble ballast with a key-bound serial sits on the buoy, listed on a board. Auditors check beacon drift against the reef chart; excess drift or a reused serial burns the bond. The first fee is 30 credits, the kth is 30+6(k-1), the 1000th is 6024, so 1000 fake identities pay 3,027,000 in fees plus 75,000 locked. A rented-buoy ring fails: a rented buoy is already on the board, so a second claim burns both bonds. An honest operator pays 30 once and recovers the bond after audit.
